title: CMU Resource Guide: resource record
description: One record per resource or space. The site renders resource pages, category pages, comparison cards and the guided flow from these records. Fields come from the Milestone 1 content audit (KAN-23) and US3/US4/US8.

id.description: Stable key used in URLs (resource.html?id=...). Lowercase words joined by hyphens. Never change it once published.

officialName.description: The name exactly as the office writes it on its own page.

aliases.description: Old, informal or outline names that should still match in search, e.g. "Neurospicy Support Group".

provider.description: The office or program that runs it, e.g. "CaPS". Shown small; the site organizes by need, not by office.

kind.description: "service" for something you use or book; "space" for a place you go (low-sensory spaces, US4).

summary.description: One or two plain-language sentences: what it helps with.

whoFor.description: Who can use it, in plain language, including limits such as "students living in Pennsylvania".

needTags.description: Need categories this record appears under. One record, many tags, so there are no drifting copies. Slugs must match the category list (KAN-25).

format.description: How students take part. Used for filters and comparison cards.

cost.description: "Free" or the cost, with any fees such as late-cancellation charges.

limits.description: Caps or rules, e.g. "12 scheduled sessions per academic year".

steps.description: Ordered, concrete actions to connect, rendered as a numbered list. Spaces can use one step, e.g. "Walk in; no booking needed."

booking.description: The single main way to start. Shown as the top button or link on the resource page.

value.description: URL, phone number or email address. Omit for walk-in or none.

locations.description: Where it happens. A list because some offices have more than one site (CaPS). Use virtual: true for online-only.

contacts.description: Who answers questions: the office line first, then any named person such as a group facilitator.

prepare.description: What to have ready: logins, documents, drafts, time. Leave empty only when there is truly nothing to prepare (e.g. a walk-in space).

script.description: Optional sample words for the call or email.

expect.description: What happens after reaching out: wait time, session length, who you meet, what happens next.

schedule.description: Time-bound info (session dates, weekly hours). Keep the text short and always link the live schedule.

sourceUrls.description: Official pages this record was checked against.

lastVerified.description: Date the record was last checked against its sources (YYYY-MM-DD). Shown on the page.

status.description: active = show it; unverified = keep in the file but hide from the site; discontinued = hide and keep for history.

internalNotes.description: Team-only notes, e.g. an open question. Never rendered on the site.
